_about: What the cross-platform run (parity/run.mjs) may find different between platforms, beyond the words in src/lib/platform.js (those are neutralised automatically). Every rule names a feature registered in parity/platform-branches.json. A line that differs and is not covered here FAILS the run. 'match' is a regular expression tested against one visible line of text.

rules.why: Docker shows who is signed in and a Sign out button.
Web and desktop have one implicit user, so the account line just says where the plan is.
The avatar shows the first two letters of the signed-in email. Letters only: two digits are the issues badge, which must still be compared.
With no email the avatar shows two dots.
The sign-up screen exists on Docker only.

knownIssues.why: Docker numbers requirement slots in the degree-spec order (CSC1020, CSC1300, MATH1910, ENGL1010, HIST2010), while web and desktop keep the older slot ids from the retired hosted database (ENGL1010 first), and a semester lists its courses by slot id. Which order students should see is a product and data decision (the spec order is the department's map). The courses in each semester are identical.
